name: bitcount
notes: popcnt+clz+ctz over a dense sweep of 1..n. VL exposes all three as width-directed free functions; Rust has count_ones/leading_zeros/trailing_zeros; Python has int.bit_count()/bit_length(). JS has only Math.clz32, so popcount is the standard SWAR emulation and ctz is 31-clz32(v & -v) — that is the idiomatic JS spelling and the extra work is a genuine finding, not a rigged race. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: rustc's default target is baseline x86-64 (no POPCNT/LZCNT/BMI1), so `rustc -O` emits SWAR while wasmtime compiles for the HOST and emits the real instructions. The `rustc -O -C target-cpu=native` column is the like-for-like comparison here. The sweep is written `for i in 0..n` with v = i+1 rather than `for i in 1..=n`, because Rust's inclusive range costs ~1.3x on its own and would have made the Rust number an artifact.

audit.vlWinIsAToolchainArtifact: MEASURED the like-for-like column the existing note asks for: rustc -O (baseline x86-64, SWAR popcount) 217.9ms, rustc -O -C target-cpu=native (real POPCNT/LZCNT/TZCNT) 151.2ms, VL 174.2ms. So 'VL beats Rust here' is TRUE only against the handicapped baseline build; against a host-tuned Rust, Rust wins 1.15x. wasmtime compiles for the HOST, so the shipped comparison is host-tuned VL vs baseline-tuned Rust. Do not publish the VL win without this column.
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
